comments.author: codetrotter
comments.story_title: Dithering Process, Return of the Obra Dinn (2017)
comments.why_zh: 艺术家谈受限调色板与艺术灵感。
comments.text_zh: 这是在 Reddit 的一个帖子里看到的。HN 之前也讨论过，但我觉得值得再发一次。之前的讨论：[LINK] 在那次讨论里，好几个人说他们更喜欢非稳定化的抖动，还争辩说老式 1-bit Mac 上“本来就是这样”。“原始效果才是它该有的样子，也是老式 1-bit 图形电脑上会呈现的样子。”一位评论者说。我觉得这些评论是只见树木不见森林。重点不是忠实复刻，而是艺术灵感和唤起某种感受。也可以看看艺术家 Mark Ferrari 的演讲“8 Bit & '8 Bitish' Graphics - Outside the Box”。[VIDEO] 如果你人为地把限制加得太死，你的游戏会受损，没人会想玩。反过来，如果你能向过去致意、带出怀旧感，同时又承认我们已经有了进步，并把这种进步融入游戏，那就有可能做出真正好玩的游戏。
comments.text: Came across this in a thread on Reddit. It’s been discussed on HN before as well but I think it’s worthy of being resubmitted. Previous discussion: [LINK] In that discussion multiple people said that they preferred the non-stabilized dithering, and they argued that that is “how it was” on the old 1-bit Macs. “The original effect is how it's supposed to look and how it would have looked on an old computer with 1-bit graphics.” says one commenter. I think these comments are missing the forest for the trees. It’s not about faithful recreation, it’s about artistic inspiration and invoking certain feelings. See also the talk “8 Bit & ‘8 Bitish’ Graphics - Outside the Box” by artist Mark Ferrari. [VIDEO] If you artificially constrain yourself too much, your game will suffer and no-one will want to play it. On the other hand, if you can give a nod to the past and a feeling of nostalgia but at the same time acknowledge that we have had progress, and incorporate that progress in your game, then there is potential for a game that is actually fun to play.

comments.author: kick
comments.story_title: A Pixel Artist Renounces Pixel Art (2015)
comments.why_zh: 展示早期 PC 像素艺术与色彩循环。
comments.quote_zh: 比如看看 Mark Ferrari 的这个演讲
comments.text_zh: 我不同意这个说法！早期的个人电脑也有像素艺术，而且当年用像素艺术做出的东西令人惊叹。比如看看 Mark Ferrari 的这个演讲：[VIDEO] [LINK] 看看他在这个 demo 里做的色彩循环：太惊人了。我推荐看看“May - Jungle Waterfall - Rain”，感受一下有多惊艳。那不是 gif，而是一张单图，只是让颜色轮转。那是为了应对存储限制。你能想象吗？早期 PC 和应用的技术同样值得保存。那条推文里展示的艺术也很惊人，但那不是一回事！那是完全不同的东西，约束条件也完全不同。
comments.text: I don't agree with that! Early personal computers also had pixel art, and it was mind-blowing what was done with it. Watch this talk from Mark Ferrari, for example: [VIDEO] [LINK] Check out what he did with color cycling in this demo: it's amazing. I recommend looking at "May - Jungle Waterfall - Rain" to see how amazing this is. That's not a gif, it's a single image, just rotating the colors. That was to deal with storage constraints. Can you imagine? The techniques of early PC and applications are worth saving , too. The art shown in that tweet is amazing, too, but it's not the same thing! It's an entirely different thing, with entirely different constraints.

comments.text: There's a lot of stuff available but the problem is knowing what to look for. For example, the book "Commodore: A Company on the Edge" chronicles quite a bit of Commodore lore, and there are numerous resources for both Amiga and C64 online. Too many to mention, really, and lots of them are heavily specialized. CSDb[0] for the C64 demo and cracking scene, for example. I also recommend The Early History of Smalltalk[1] by Alan Kay himself and Mark Ferrari's talk[2] on creating pixel art for LucasArts games. [0] [LINK] [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.text: You might be interested in this GCD talk. The speaker was an artist on various classic adventure games. I found it really interesting how he considered himself a traditional artist and doesn't really like computers at all. The things they achieved with pallette switching were unbelievable, especially considering the limitations of their tools. It's crazy how he managed to do this stuff just in basic paint programs. Some HNers will be horrified (just write some code!) but I think it's really inspiring. [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 8 Bit 与“8 Bitish”图形——跳出框框 [VIDEO] > 在 GDC 2016 的这场演讲中，Terrible Toybox 的 Mark Ferrari 讨论并演示了他绘制 8 位游戏图形的一些技术，包括他广受赞誉的方法：利用色彩循环和调色板移位，在不使用逐帧动画的情况下创建复杂而逼真的背景动画效果 色彩循环的失落艺术——用颜色做动画 [LINK] > 色彩循环诞生于硬件限制，但从中产生了一些美丽的艺术作品，它们构成了 80 年代和 90 年代的特征。在这段视频中，我们将进一步了解这种效果是如何产生的，并亲身感受用它创作出的美丽艺术作品。
comments.text: 8 Bit & '8 Bitish' Graphics-Outside the Box [VIDEO] > In this GDC 2016 talk, Terrible Toybox's Mark Ferrari discusses and demonstrate some of his techniques for drawing 8 bit game graphics, including his celebrated methods for use of color cycling and pallet shifting to create complex and realistic background animation effects without frame-animation The lost art of color cycling - Animating with color [LINK] > Color cycling was born out of hardware restrictions but out of it came some beautiful artworks that characterized the 80s and 90s. In this video we will learn more about how this effect was produced and experience first hand the beautiful artwork created with it.
